# asyntai_webhook (Resource)

A webhook: Asyntai sends a signed POST request to your address when an event happens, for example a new chat or a captured lead. The API has no update call for webhooks, so a change creates a new webhook with a new secret.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "asyntai_webhook" "leads" {
  website_id = asyntai_website.shop.id
  url        = "https://hooks.example.com/asyntai"
  events     = ["lead.captured", "ticket.created"]
}

output "webhook_secret" {
  value     = asyntai_webhook.leads.secret
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `events` (Set of String) Events to send: `message.received`, `conversation.started`, `escalation.requested`, `takeover.started`, `lead.captured`, `ticket.created`.
- `url` (String) Address that receives the events. Must start with `http://` or `https://`.

### Optional

- `website_id` (String) Id of the website whose events are sent. Defaults to the primary website.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the webhook was created.
- `id` (String) Webhook id.
- `is_active` (Boolean) Whether Asyntai still sends events to the address.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) Signing secret (`whsec_...`). Use it to check that a request comes from Asyntai. The API shows it only once, at create; an imported webhook has no secret in state.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by webhook id. The signing secret is shown only at create, so an imported webhook has none in state.
terraform import asyntai_webhook.leads 7c9e6679-7425-40de-944b-e07fc1f90ae7
```
